## Overview

This project turns a plain-text resource list into a searchable front end for curated data science references across R, Python, statistics, visualization, research workflows, and life sciences.

It is intentionally both a curation project and a small product-engineering exercise: define a lightweight schema, keep the source easy to edit, and ship a fast browsing experience without introducing a heavyweight backend.

## What This Project Includes

- A hand-curated catalog stored in `resources.txt`, with each entry typed, categorized, and optionally annotated with a short description
- An R step that turns the catalog into a native Quarto listing at render time — text search, sorting, category filtering, and pagination included, with no custom JavaScript
- A low-friction contribution workflow based on small YAML blocks and documented pull requests

```{r resource-catalog-items}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| output: false
source(here::here("resources.R"))

resources <- parse_resources_md(here::here("resources.txt"))
write_listing_items(resources, here::here("resources-items.yml"))
```

::: {#resources}
:::

:::: {.callout-note}
## Contributing
Want to add a resource? Edit `resources.txt` and open a PR on [GitHub](https://github.com/antoinelucasfra/resources-catalog). Each resource is a small YAML block:

```yaml
---
title: "Resource Title"
type: Book
link: https://example.com
language: R
category: "Statistics;Tutorial"
description: "A brief one-sentence description shown on the card and in search."
---
```

The `description` field is optional but recommended — it appears on the card and is included in the full-text search.

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/antoinelucasfra/resources-catalog/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for the full guide, including how resources are synced from Google Keep.
